slides.page_title: Gateway API & Choosing a Service Type

items: Role-oriented, typed, portable CRDs instead of annotations
GatewayClass is infra kind; Gateway is a listener plus TLS
HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute and TCPRoute carry the rules
Platform team owns the Gateway, app teams own Routes
ReferenceGrant makes cross-namespace attachment explicit
Header matching, weighted splits, mirroring: all first-class
Weighted splits make canary and blue/green a spec feature
Ingress stays supported; new build-outs go Gateway API

blocks.title: Mesh Overlap
items: Mesh adds mTLS, retries, circuit breaking, east-west L7
Ingress is north-south; they solve different directions
Most power for the most ops cost — not a routing fix
iptables mode picks a backend at random
IPVS mode runs real scheduling algorithms
Pick one with the `--ipvs-scheduler` flag
lc suits long-lived, uneven connections
sh gives client stickiness without cookies
Omit the flag and you get rr

blocks.title: Scope
items: The scheduler is set per kube-proxy, not per Service
Restart kube-proxy for a change to take effect
Verify live tables with `ipvsadm -Ln`
`loadBalancerClass` names which controller handles it
Two LB implementations can share one cluster
Unset means the default provider claims the Service
Controllers ignore classes they do not own
The field is immutable once the Service exists
Migrating classes means recreating the Service

blocks.title: Layering
items: LoadBalancer contains NodePort contains ClusterIP
Each type adds to the one below it
It never replaces the layer underneath

blocks.title: One Object, Three Layers
blocks.text: Every LoadBalancer still owns a NodePort and a ClusterIP underneath it.

slides.page_title: DNS Search Lists, ndots & Default Backend

items: Every Pod gets a generated `/etc/resolv.conf`
It names CoreDNS and carries a search list
Node domains may be appended to that list
`<ns>.svc.cluster.local` sits first in the list
Then `svc.cluster.local`, then `cluster.local`
Short names resolve by walking that order
Under five dots counts as an unqualified name
Unqualified names try every suffix first
`api.github.com` carries only two dots
Three to four failed lookups before the answer
Real added latency on every external call
Multiplies CoreDNS query load cluster-wide

blocks.title: Cures
items: A trailing dot skips the search list entirely
Lower ndots per Pod with `dnsConfig`
NodeLocal DNSCache absorbs the misses
`defaultBackend` catches everything no rule matched
Without it you get the controller's stock 404
Point it at a branded error or landing Service

blocks.title: Own The Miss
blocks.text: An unmatched host or path is a routing decision — do not leave it to the controller.

items: Controls how the Service allocates IP addresses
Three modes: Single, Prefer, Require
Set at creation; immutable afterwards
Explicit list of allowed IP families
Order matters for PreferDualStack
Must match cluster CNI capabilities

blocks.title: Cluster Prereqs
items: CNI must support the requested family
Node must have valid IP addresses
Check `kubectl get nodes -o wide`
Check Service status for assigned IPs
Test connectivity with `ping6` or `curl`
Verify DNS records for both families

blocks.title: Migration Path
blocks.text: Start with PreferDualStack, then move to RequireDualStack once stable.
